questions.question: A nurse is asked by a physician to witness an informed consent form for a patient who received IV lorazepam 20 minutes ago and is now drowsy and slurring words. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Guide the drowsy patient's hand to sign the form
Refuse to have the patient sign while sedated and notify the physician that the patient currently lacks decision-making capacity
Sign the patient's name on their behalf
Ask another patient in the next bed to witness the signature

questions.explanation: A patient under the influence of sedatives, narcotics, or anesthesia lacks legal capacity to give valid informed consent. The nurse must halt the signing and inform the physician (who may postpone or obtain surrogate/emergency consent if legally applicable).
questions.hint: Evaluate whether a sedated, drowsy patient possesses valid legal decision-making capacity.
questions.subject: Ethics & Legal Issues

questions.question: According to the International Council of Nurses (ICN) Code of Ethics (revised 2021), which four principal elements outline the standards of ethical nursing conduct?

options.text: Assessment, Diagnosis, Planning, Evaluation
Nurses and Patients/People, Nurses and Practice, Nurses and the Profession, Nurses and Global Health
Duty, Breach, Causation, Damages
Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability

questions.explanation: The ICN Code of Ethics is structured around four core elements: (1) Nurses and Patients or other People requiring care, (2) Nurses and Practice, (3) Nurses and the Profession, and (4) Nurses and Global Health.
questions.hint: Look for the four broad domains defining a nurse's ethical relationships from individual patients to global health.

questions.question: An unconscious victim of a road traffic accident with severe internal bleeding arrives in the emergency department alone, with no family reachable. The trauma surgeon orders immediate life-saving laparotomy. Under what legal principle can surgery proceed without signed written consent?

options.text: Informed refusal
Implied consent (emergency doctrine)
Express written consent
Vicarious consent

questions.explanation: Under the emergency doctrine (implied consent), the law presumes that a reasonable person would consent to immediate life-saving treatment when unconscious or incapacitated and no surrogate is available to delay urgent care.
questions.hint: Name the type of consent legally presumed when an unconscious patient requires immediate life-saving intervention.
questions.subject: Ethics & Legal Issues

questions.question: A nurse administers a medication that was NOT prescribed because the nurse skipped checking the patient's wristband and MAR, but the patient fortunately suffers no harm or adverse effect. Can the patient successfully win a legal malpractice lawsuit?

options.text: Yes, because any mistake automatically wins a malpractice verdict
No, because actual harm/damages (one of the four required elements of malpractice) did not occur—though the nurse still faces hospital disciplinary/incident review
Yes, under the tort of libel
No, because nurses cannot be sued for medication errors

questions.explanation: All four elements (Duty, Breach, Causation, Damages) must be proven to win a civil malpractice lawsuit. Without actual harm/damages, civil malpractice fails—though the breach still requires an incident report and professional accountability.
questions.hint: Check all four mandatory elements of malpractice and notice which critical element is missing here.
questions.subject: Ethics & Legal Issues

questions.question: A competent patient refuses an ordered nasogastric tube insertion and insists on leaving the hospital Against Medical Advice (AMA). Which actions should the nurse take? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Notify the physician so the physician can explain the specific medical risks of leaving AMA
Ask the patient to sign the AMA release form (and document objectively if the patient refuses to sign)
Remove IV cannulas/hospital lines safely before departure and ensure the patient receives safe discharge info if willing
Physically block the door until the hospital bill is paid in full

questions.explanation: Competent adults have the right to leave AMA. The nurse notifies the provider to explain risks, asks the patient to sign the AMA form (documenting objectively if refused), removes IV lines safely, and NEVER detains the patient (which would be false imprisonment).
questions.hint: Respect autonomy while protecting legal documentation and avoiding false imprisonment.
questions.subject: Ethics & Legal Issues

questions.question: A nurse is caring for a patient in a medico-legal case (MLC) admitted after an alleged physical assault. Which legal nursing responsibilities apply to handling the patient's clothing and potential forensic evidence?

options.text: Wash the bloodstained clothes immediately and return them to the family
Preserve clothing and biological specimens intact in separate labeled paper bags and maintain a strict documented chain of custody for police/forensic authorities
Discard torn clothing in the yellow biomedical waste bin immediately
Give the patient's clothing to a news reporter for verification

questions.explanation: In medico-legal cases (MLC), preserving evidence in paper bags (plastic traps moisture and degrades DNA) and maintaining an unbroken, signed chain of custody is a critical legal nursing duty.
questions.hint: Think about how forensic evidence must be preserved and tracked from bedside to police custody.
questions.subject: Ethics & Legal Issues

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A nurse must maintain an active, valid registration with the State Nursing Council / INC to practice legally as a Nursing Officer.
Reason (R): Nursing licensure exists primarily to protect the public by ensuring that practitioners meet minimum standards of education, competence, and safe practice.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.explanation: [AIIMS NORCET / FON Legal Concept] Practicing nursing without a valid license is illegal (a criminal offense). Licensure laws exist primarily to safeguard public health and safety by verifying minimum professional competency.
questions.hint: Consider both the legal requirement for nursing registration and the primary public-protection purpose of licensure.
